title: skills(objectstack-data): evals 11, 12 and 14 of objects-fields-relationships.json list must_contain literals their expected_output lacks
body:
domain:skills#1 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5pjSPT7ui2EUcunaVb

Filing gate: ① (named landing point, found by the dev and confirmed by the contract review of PR #33394, card #32392, comment 6882437074, follow-up 2)

**What is wrong.** In `skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json` on `main`, three evals list `must_contain` literals that their own `expected_output` does not contain, so the reference answer fails its own grader: eval 11 lacks `type: 'select'` and `type: 'state_machine'`; eval 12 lacks `type: 'summary'` and `type: 'formula'`; eval 14 lacks `label: '公司名称'` and `value: 'active'`. The evals README requires every `must_contain` literal to appear in `expected_output`. No repo check reads the shape of `skills/objectstack-*/evals` (`check:skill-eval-tokens` covers objectui only), which is how they drifted.

**Reach.** Measured by script over the file at PR #33394's head (the PR does not touch these evals).

**Business reason.** The data skill's eval harness measures whether an agent answers correctly; an eval whose reference answer fails its own literals cannot tell a right answer from a wrong one.

**Reader who acts.** The `domain:skills` seat: fix the three `expected_output`s (or the literals, whichever is wrong against `main`), one changeset (`'@objectstack/skills': patch`, `Clause-②: no`). Optionally name in the card's PR whether a shape check over these eval files is worth a separate card.

**Dedupe.** `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue objects-fields-relationships must_contain`: 8 hits, the only open one is #32392 (adds eval 17). `… eval expected_output must_contain literal`: 22 hits, none open on these evals.
